why: Every R5 finding was a pad with the right net assignment sitting on an isolated copper island. Six gates said PASS because they checked pad-net assignments rather than continuity. A bench that solves the netlist as a circuit cannot make that mistake -- an island has no current path -- so R5 is the cheapest proof that Phase 1 works at all.

entries.title: boost inductor L1 isolated on its BAT+ side
entries.must_report: no current path from BAT+ through L1 to the IP5306 switching node, therefore no +5V on battery power while USB still works -- the asymmetry is the signature

entries.title: IP5306 BAT+ bulk cap C18 isolated
entries.must_report: C18 contributes zero capacitance to BAT+, so the BAT+ transient response is that of an undecoupled input

entries.title: IP5306 VBUS decoupling cap C17 isolated
entries.must_report: C17 contributes zero capacitance to VBUS

entries.title: every button's pull-up and debounce cap on a floating island
entries.must_report: BTN_A has no external pull-up in the circuit: the pin's idle level depends entirely on the ESP32 internal pull, and the debounce RC time constant is zero
entries.note: The board is functionally operable this way because the firmware enables internal pull-ups, which is exactly why this survived. The bench must report the electrical fact and must NOT report a broken button.

entries.title: SW_BOOT not connected to the BTN_SELECT network
entries.must_report: holding SW_BOOT across reset does not pull GPIO0 low, so the download-mode strapping sequence cannot be entered from the buttons
entries.note: Mutation targets pad 2: datasheet_specs declares SW_BOOT pad 1 unconnected and the board puts the signal terminal on pad 2, so detaching pad 1 would be a no-op and the entry would look uncatchable when it had never been applied.

entries.title: menu combo diode D1 isolated from BTN_START and BTN_SELECT
entries.must_report: pressing SW13 pulls neither BTN_START nor BTN_SELECT low, so the one-button menu combo does nothing
